slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 3:15: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.
slides.body: “And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.”
slides.heading: Gen 3:15

slides.alt_text: Slide 2: Is the serpent Satan? Genesis says one of the woman’s descendants will strike the serpent’s head. Christians often read this as Jesus defeating Satan.
slides.body: Genesis says one of the woman’s descendants will strike the serpent’s head. Christians often read this as Jesus defeating Satan.
slides.heading: Is the serpent Satan?

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: Why Christians connect them Later parts of the Bible call the devil “the ancient serpent” and say Jesus came to destroy his work. So the Christian connection makes sense when the whole Bible is read together.
slides.body: Later parts of the Bible call the devil “the ancient serpent” and say Jesus came to destroy his work. So the Christian connection makes sense when the whole Bible is read together.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Slide 4: But that connection comes later Genesis names neither Jesus nor Satan. The story also explains why humans and snakes are enemies. Later writers give the serpent a larger meaning, but Genesis itself does not clearly predict Jesus defeating Satan.
slides.body: Genesis names neither Jesus nor Satan. The story also explains why humans and snakes are enemies. Later writers give the serpent a larger meaning, but Genesis itself does not clearly predict Jesus defeating Satan.
slides.heading: But that connection comes later

title: Does Genesis predict Jesus defeating Satan?
